passage:
A seaside town noticed its beach was becoming smaller. Storms and rising water had taken away sand year by year.
Some hotel owners wanted to bring in more sand. Scientists warned that this might help only for a short time if waves and construction kept changing the coast.
The town held meetings with residents, engineers, and environmental experts. They discussed sea walls, restored dunes, and limits on building near the shore.
There was no easy answer.
The beach was not just a tourist place. It was a living edge between land and sea. Protecting it required more than adding sand. It required respecting movement.
